title: Logic Blocks Arcade
intro: Five rounds on sequence, decisions and loops. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: "Turn right, then move forward" vs "move forward, then turn right." Are these the same program?
options: No — order changes where the robot ends up
Yes, order never matters in a sequence
They're only different if a loop is involved
rounds.explain: A sequence runs in the exact order written — swap two steps and you can get a completely different result.

rounds.prompt: An If block's condition is false. What happens to its 'then' branch?
options: It's skipped — only the else branch (if any) runs
rounds.explain: The 'then' branch is specifically for the true case. A false condition skips straight to else, or does nothing if there is no else.

rounds.prompt: Match each shape to what it does.

pairs.right: Picks a branch based on a condition

rounds.explain: Every algorithm you'll ever write is built from these — even the most complex real robot program.

rounds.prompt: Why is 'repeat forever' with nothing that can change the situation inside it risky?
options: It never ends on its own — nothing inside it can break the pattern
rounds.explain: Without a decision or exit condition, an unlimited loop truly has no way to stop by itself.

rounds.prompt: `repeat forever: if wall ahead: turn, else: move forward` — why does this generalise to a maze it's never seen, unlike a hardcoded sequence?
options: It reacts to whatever it actually senses, rather than memorising one fixed path
It uses fewer blocks, which always generalises better
It doesn't generalise any better than a hardcoded sequence
rounds.explain: A reactive program built from a loop and a decision responds to the real situation in front of it, not a memorised route.
